openQuestions: Each voice file reads, in order: the talk title, each chapter title and script, the three check questions with their options, then the answers with the reason, then a one-line goodbye. If the app wants to play the questions as a separate quiz, cut the voice files at the line 'Three questions to check yourself' (Hindi: 'अब खुद को जाँचने के लिए तीन सवाल').

All spoken text has numbers in words, including titles, so the freedom-struggle titles read 'part one: from eighteen fifty-seven to nineteen nineteen'. Claude Code may want to add a short display title with digits (for example 'Freedom struggle 1: 1857–1919') for the app list.
minutes is an estimate from the English word count plus the check section, at about 140 words a minute; it can be replaced with the real mp3 length after recording.
freedom-struggle-1857-1919 and freedom-struggle-1919-1947 are a pair; part two opens by pointing back to part one. They could be linked as a series in the app.
The Partition passage in freedom-struggle-1919-1947 deliberately gives no casualty or displacement figure, because estimates vary widely; it says 'many millions' displaced and 'large numbers' killed.
